On the topic of introducing new players, there are two approaches I narrow myself down to: Running a demo (e.g., at a Con) or just introducing someone.

When we're at a Con, I really want to make sure the game goes quickly and smoothly, as there are (almost) always other people wanting to play at the table. In those cases, I'll (almost) exclusively play Legacy, as he makes everyone else better, makes the game more enjoyable for the other heroes, and makes the game faster. Heroes like OX and AA, while they help everyone and can similarly improve their game experience, take far longer on their turns, significantly slowing down the game. (And yes, it really doesn't matter how well I know the hero, they just take longer - it's the nature of the hero that they are going to take longer than Legacy, as they have more things to do every turn.)

Now, if I'm just introducing someone to the game, I'll generally follow the comments others have made: Legacy first, but if they get the concepts in general I'll show them someone more complex who will still support, like AA or OX. There usually isn't a "rush" on those games, so that constraint isn't as big of a deal.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Drakossozh:

As an aside (sorry to go off-topic, a bit), I've been trying to play Adept for months now, and I always seem to fall short. Can't seem to get him going the way people describe him (or even, the way I've seen him get going), even when I read Flamethrower's wonderful wonderful guide. Er, any tips? D:

That depends, if you are just having bad card luck, then shuffle your cards differently and keep at it.

If your cards keep getting destroyed, then you will have to play the "I'm not a one-man-band" adept and do what you can.

If you just don't seem to be using him well, remember a couple of things:  

  1.  Just because you can chain doesn't mean you should.  Sometimes letting a player us their power is better than that last instrument you can play.

  2.  Adept is really dependent upon the other heroes doing something.  Make sure you are helping the right people each round.

  3.  Know the match you are in.  If you really want to get set up and roll try playing against Grand Warlord Voss, he doesn't destroy your cards and he takes a while to kill.  Also some players are better at being helped by Adept than others, Bunker can benefit a ton from extra card plays if he has the cards before he drops into turret, the damage reduction is epic on Stealth Bot or Legacy with lead from the front (stealth Bot is incredible at -2 damage taken, or -3 if you can pull it off), and almost everyone benefits from +damage or reduction, and the occasional extra card play is great.

  4.  Make sure your team knows what you can do.  Playing Unload or Salvage Yard out of turn is awesome, if Expat is going to Unload, tell her to play two cards or use a regular gun and you'll let her unload on your turn.

  5.  Go for it.  Never hold back or worry about what is going to happen.  I have a friend who keeps trying to get the ideal set-up (he has one in mind) and he ends up never using Adept well because of it.  Do the best you can each turn, and don't worry about building toward a specific goal.  You'll get there if the game allows.  Kind of like Nightmist, Bunker or AZ:  if you spend your time trying to get one exact set-up then you will waste a lot of your games, just do the best you can.

posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
Drakossozh:

As an aside (sorry to go off-topic, a bit), I've been trying to play Adept for months now, and I always seem to fall short. Can't seem to get him going the way people describe him (or even, the way I've seen him get going), even when I read Flamethrower's wonderful wonderful guide. Er, any tips? D:

First up, you've got to be really flexible.  You can't walk into a game with AA expecting "I'm going to buff damage for everyone" or "I'm going to facilitate card play/draw."  The one thing you can't control is what songs you have and, while you have a good deal of card draw, you can't guarantee having the precise one you want.  Much like Mister Fixer, you've got to go with the flow…

Second, your play order:  first up is always a song, either by itself or via Arcane Cadence.  With no songs in play, even your base power is shut down.  But, considering the number of songs in the deck and your ability to find them with Arcane Cadence, you'll likely have one very soon.  If your song is a Harmony or a Rhythm, your next best play is likely an instrument:  specifically the instrument that lets you play Perform and Accompany of whichever you've played.  That gives you two benefits to your party in one power phase.  If your song is a Melody, sling down a second song before fishing for instruments, to get maximum benefit.

Silver Shadow is almost always worth playing:  the only exception is that if you don't have a song with an Accompany text out and you don't need the additional card draw.  But, as long as you have an Accompany text to play with it, don't leave it in your hand.  

Once you have a basic "set" to play:  either Perform/Perform or Perform/Accompany, look at expansion.  The easiest way to expand, I've found is from a Harmony/Harmony or Rhythm/Rhythm into a Melody/Harmony or Melody/Rhythm.  Plus, Sarabande of Destruction is just phenomenal, so I tend to favor finding it.  That said, if you went Rhythm/Rhythm via Xu's Bell, it may benefit you more to go Rhythm/Harmony.  Don't forget, as well, that you can use the same card multiple times, once you've chained some powers together.  Double-dipping the same card can lead to some phenomenal results–and don't forget your base power!  An extra Perform text can be pretty spectacular.

Polyphoric Flare seems like a bad option sometimes, but unless you're really hurting on hp, you can easily restore those lost 2 hp and the power usage is almost always worth it.  It can be especially good early in a game, when your hp are relatively high and you've just got down your first instrument.  Again, don't be afraid to double-dip on cards.  

Now, I'm not the AA expert by any sense–one of my Friday night game group utterly adores him, and plays Adept almost exclusively (with a smattering of Chrono-Ranger, when he wants to deal damage).  But, with some additional games under my belt with AA, his complexity becomes an awesome puzzle to figure out!

I did have a song in-hand but it was Cedistic Dissonance, probably the only song that's utterly useless if you start off with it, since there's no way you can both play it and use its effect (destroy an instrument to destroy any non-character card in the game) on the first turn. I did later nuke my Harp to take out the Flagship but the game was over in about four or five rounds - too much Minion damage, not enough good cards coming out :(.

I do recall a game we had, ages ago, against Citizen Dawn in which I never had more than about four cards out at once - something like Alacritous Subdominant, another song or two, and an instrument, but I was able to chain them in such a way that I could do something useful every round and we ended up winning the fight :).

Knowing other character's decks can help when playing the Adept, actually, as you'll know, for example, that Unity does well with extra plays (to get out her bots), Expatriette likes extra draws (for her guns and ammo), and so on. You can decide which character you let take which action from your various songs and hopefully get the best effect from them. I've also had a game where Fanatic had used Wrathful Retribution on her turn. On mine, I was able to get her to put it back on top of her deck (Vernal Sonata), then draw it (Counterpoint Bulwark). I can't remember whether I then let her play it again as well (Alacritous Subdominant or Inventive Preparation) or whether that occurred on her turn. Much nuking occurred, either way ;).

Finally, the one thing I give the lowest priority when playing the Adept is dealing damage. He has exactly two songs (well, four if you count both copies of those two songs) which deal damage - Syncopated Onslaught (Accompany text deals one Sonic damage to a target), and Scherzo of Frost and Flame (deal one target one fire damage and then deal one target one cold damage…or the other way round, I can't remember). I can remember one long game against…I think it was Akash'Bhuta but may possibly have been Gloomweaver, in which I dealt one hit of damage the entire game, and that was the killing blow on the villain just because I could >:). In general, I'll look at whatever thing needs to be done in the game the most right now, and then which character could do it and how, and then which effect(s) I could use to make that thing happen ASAP.

It took me a few games to get the hang of the Adept, but once I'd sort of learnt his deck a bit, I…well, got the hang of him, and he went from being "Hrmm, that guy's kind of complicated…" to being my favourite character :). Note that I don't play him every game or anything - I tend to play him in games that tend to be a bit longer, so I hopefully have more time to get out my stuff. I'm unlikely to pick him against Iron Legacy, for example, or someone like La Capitan who has a million horribel cards and breaks all my stuff :P.
